messages.author: 970bb92277d806ae
messages.subject: Bernoulli - Simple Model with 5 coins
parts:
I have an issue with this estimation. I can't understand why Stan is not running.

This model is simple, just a bernoulli distribution of 5 coins.


Could you help me?


This is the code (in R):


# Generate data for 5 coins ( g) and the values (y : head(0) or tail(1) )
tt_dados <- data.frame(y=c(
  rbinom(300, 1, .234),
  rbinom(300, 1, .728),
  rbinom(300, 1, .534),
  rbinom(300, 1, .349),
  rbinom(300, 1, .765)),
  g=c(rep(1,300),
      rep(2,300),
      rep(3,300),
      rep(4,300),
      rep(5,300))
)

# Prepare data for Stan
t_dados <- list(
  y=tt_dados$y, 
  g=tt_dados$g)


# Model
stan_st <- "
  data {
    int y[1500];
    int g[1500];
  }
  parameters {
    real x[5];
  }
  model {
    for (i in 1:1500) {
      y[i] ~ bernoulli(x[g[i]]);
    }
    for (i in 1:5) {
      x[i] ~ normal(0, 1);
    }
  }
  
  "
fit <- stan(model_code=stan_st, data=t_dados, iter=1500, warmup=100, thin=10, chains=2)

"

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Bernoulli - Simple Model with 5 coins
parts:
You need to declare

real<lower=0, upper=1> x[5];

because the parameter x is constrained to be between
0 and 1. See the intro to Stan programming in the manual
for full details.

Then you have to make sure that the indexes aren't out of
bound and you should be good to go.

I don't think your prior makes much sense, but that's not
why the code's not running.

- Bob
